player.keys_help: Space or K play/pause · ← → 5 s · J / L 10 s · , and . one frame · Home / End · I / O mark the export start and end
player.seg.unknown: Length unknown: this clip couldn't be read
player.veil.locked_body: Decrypt the event above to watch it here.
player.veil.bad_body: The file is probably cut short. That happens when the USB drive comes out while the car is still writing.
player.range.label: Range
player.range.sel_note: {len} selected. Tap Start or End to move it to the playhead, or press I / O.
player.range.sel_invalid: The end has to come after the start.
player.export.overlay_sub: Speed, power and battery from TeslaMate, plus gear, steering and accelerator from the clip itself.
player.export.no_libass: Not available: this ffmpeg was built without libass, so exports come out without the overlay.
player.export.encoder_sw: Encoder: {name}, software, so exports take longer
player.report.unavailable: No overlay: this ffmpeg has no libass
player.report.no_telemetry: No overlay: neither TeslaMate nor the clip has telemetry for this range
player.report.sei_only: TeslaMate couldn't be reached, so the overlay only shows what the clip recorded
player.report.dropped_unreadable: {time} left out: the {cams} clip couldn't be read
player.report.short: The {cam} clip at {time} is {dur} s, the others {expected} s. That view freezes until the next segment.
player.evidence.title: Evidence package
player.evidence.body: The original footage, the event details, telemetry from TeslaMate and the clip as CSV, and checksums, in one ZIP for your insurer or the police.
player.evidence.note: The download starts right away. A long event can be several GB, so your browser shows how much has arrived rather than a percentage.
player.align.ok: Offset {offset} s, off by {rmse} {unit} on average across {samples} samples. Saved: the HUD and exports use it from now on.
player.align.kept: The clock offset was left as it was.
player.sei.heading: Driving data
player.missing: This clip isn't in the library any more
decrypt.title: {n} of {total} clips can't play until decrypted
decrypt.body: Your car encrypts Dashcam footage with a key tied to your Tesla account. You can decrypt it here: only the header of each clip goes to Tesla to fetch its key. The video never leaves this machine.
decrypt.token_help: This token can only fetch decryption keys. It can't control your car or read its data. OhmyTesla uses it once, in memory, and never stores it.
decrypt.keep_sub: Saved next to each clip as .mp4.enc. Delete them once the decrypted footage plays.
decrypt.preview_note: One entry per clip: the VIN, key ID, timestamp, and the wrapped and public keys from the clip's header. No video.
decrypt.busy_other: Another event is being decrypted. Try again when it's finished.
decrypt.done_kept: The encrypted originals are kept as .mp4.enc. Delete them once you're happy.
decrypt.nothing: Nothing left to decrypt in this event.
usb.import.desc_recent: Uploads these driving clips. On the server they join any RecentClips already there.
usb.import.desc_locked: These clips are encrypted. Import them, then decrypt them on the server with your Tesla account.
usb.veil.locked_body: Import this clip, then decrypt it on the server with your Tesla account.
dashcam.note.shadowed_body: The clips in {hidden} aren't shown, because the library reads {base}. Move them in there and rescan.
dashcam.note.locked_body: Not a single frame can be read from them. Usually that's encryption: since car software 2026.20, Dashcam footage is encrypted with a key tied to your Tesla account. Open the clip to decrypt it here. A copy that was cut short looks the same, so if it isn't encrypted, copy it again.
dashcam.note.skipped_body: Their names aren't a date and time the car could have written, or they couldn't be read.
dashcam.note.timeouts_title: {n} clips took too long to check
dashcam.note.timeouts_body: That's usually a slow network share, not a broken clip, so they aren't counted as unreadable. Rescan to try again.
dashcam.empty.filter: No clips of this kind yet.
sdc.heading: Dashcam
sdc.tz_why: Clip names carry the car's local time with no zone, so a wrong zone shifts every overlay and every TeslaMate lookup by whole hours. Set TESLACAM_TZ to change it.
sdc.intro: teslausb is a Raspberry Pi that takes the place of the USB drive in your car. When the car gets home, it copies new clips to this hub.
sdc.never_sub: Add the two lines below to the Pi and every run will be reported here.
sdc.error_hint: Common on 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS since car software 2025.44: the repeater and pillar clips get skipped. Reinstall teslausb on 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS (see docs/TESLAUSB.md).
sdc.copying_now: Files are being copied right now.
sdc.pending.copying: {event}: waiting for the folder to finish copying
sdc.pending.retry: {event}: the alert didn't go out, will retry {when}
sdc.hook.title: Tell the hub when a run finishes
sdc.hook.intro: Paste these two lines into teslausb_setup_variables.conf on the Pi. The hub then rescans the moment new clips land, instead of within a minute.
sdc.hook.copy_manual: Couldn't copy. The lines are selected: press Ctrl+C or ⌘C.
sdc.hook.rotate_lead: The current token stops working at once. Until the new lines are on the Pi, the hub won't hear about archive runs, though it still finds new clips within a minute.
sdc.hook.rotated: New token issued. Update the Pi.
sdc.hook.note: The token only lets the Pi ask for a rescan; it can't open anything else. Never put the portal password on the Pi: the Pi lives in the car.
sdc.hook.localhost: This page is open on the computer's own address, which the Pi can't reach. Use its LAN address instead of
sdc.pi.title: The Pi on your network
sdc.pi.intro: Optional. With its address, the hub can show how the Pi is doing and ask it to sync a Sentry event recorded in the garage. Fill in the user name and password only if you set WEB_USERNAME on the Pi.
sdc.pi.password_ph: Only if the Pi asks for one
sdc.pi.password_saved: Saved. Leave empty to keep it
sdc.pi.sync_ok: The Pi will sync once it's idle at home. It briefly disconnects the drive from the car while it does.
sdc.pi.drive_off: Drive not connected to the car
dashcam.note.timeouts_title_one: {n} clip took too long to check
player.sei.scope: Segment from {time}, as the car recorded it
sdc.pi.err_timeout: The Pi took too long to answer. Is it home and on Wi-Fi?
sdc.pi.err_connect: Couldn't reach the Pi: the address is wrong, or it's away from home.
sdc.pi.err_auth: The Pi asked for a password. Enter the teslausb web user name and password above.
sdc.pi.err_json: The Pi answered, but not with the status teslausb normally sends.
player.export.locked: Decrypt this event first: none of its clips can be read yet.
align.no_overlap: The clip and TeslaMate's data don't overlap in time.
align.no_sei: This clip doesn't carry enough telemetry (older firmware, a parked Sentry Mode clip, or encrypted), so it can't be calibrated automatically.
align.flat_speed: The speed barely changes in this clip (cruising or parked), so any offset fits. Pick a drive with some speeding up and slowing down.
align.no_telemetry: TeslaMate has too little driving data for that time (was the car moving?).
align.poor_fit: Not a reliable fit: at the best offset ({off} s) the speeds still differ by {rmse} km/h (limit {max}). The clip and TeslaMate's record may not be the same drive. The offset is unchanged.
align.no_minimum: Not a reliable fit: the best offset ({off} s) isn't clearly better than the others ({rmse} vs a median of {median} km/h). The offset is unchanged.
align.pick_car: This account has several cars: choose the car in the player first.
